notes: WebSearch could not be used for this part (the session's search budget was already spent: 200 of 200), so pages were reached directly: the campaign websites filed with the Secretary of State (as sl_websites holds them), government and school district sites, and the state DFL's list of endorsed candidates. No Republican unit's endorsement page could be found without a search (Karen Attia in Senate District 34 and KT Jacobs in House District 39B were not looked up on a party page); guessed addresses did not resolve.

Not read: attiaforsenate.org (Karen Attia's filed address) showed a bot check instead of the site, so no website is recorded for her here. bergstromfor110.org (Jesse Bergstrom's filed address) failed its certificate check (hostname mismatch; with www, a missing issuer) and was not read. www.co.houston.mn.us refused the TLS handshake (no page for the county attorney, Daniel Coogan). www.isd2142.k12.mn.us did not answer (Ron Marinaro). mncourts.gov is known to answer 403 and mn.gov shows a CAPTCHA, so nothing was looked up for Judge Robert C. Friday.

Looked up and not found on the government's own page, so nothing is recorded: Jay Samuelson (Pine County's board page lists Steve Hallan for District 1), Curtis Knutson (Polk County's page lists Warren Strandell for District 2), Joshua Iverson (Pennington County's page lists Neil Peterson for District 3), Paul Haik (the City of Chanhassen's 2026 candidates page lists him and gives no website), Logan Drews (Hibbing's council page lists Jay Hildenbrand for Ward 2), Eric Johnson (Elk River's council page lists Jennifer Wagner for Ward 4), Kris Taylor (not on the Saint Paul board's members page). The board pages of Litchfield, Cambridge-Isanti and the City of Crystal load their member lists by script and could not be read (Jordan Papke, DeEtta N. Moos; Forest Eidbo's council seat rests on his own site). Sartell-St. Stephen's district site was not found (Emily Larson).

Read and left out on purpose: jobs (sheriff's office ranks, teaching, banking), military service, schools, family, transit and joint-powers board seats listed without dates, club memberships, and endorsements by people, unions and other non-party groups. Aaron Kania's site shows a DFL badge among its supporters' logos but no sentence of his own to quote. KT Jacobs's site names no party of her own.

party_support (a key the loader does not read, in the shape parts 0, 6 and 10 use): the Senate District 43 DFL lists Forest Eidbo on its Vote page under "Letters of Support", which is not an endorsement (the verifier did not find the words "Letter of Support" on his own site's home page, so that part of the note was taken out). Kept apart from endorsed_by; whether and how it is shown is John's decision.

Clint Hooppaw: the city's page says "Served since 2011" beside the title Mayor; his own site splits it into council member 2011-2021 and mayor from 2021, which is what is recorded. Jon Wilson, KT Jacobs and Eric Johnson give lengths of service without years; the years are left as not stated.
